brief: MUFG forecasts August 2026 headline CPI at 0.32% MoM (3.3% YoY) and core CPI at 0.23% MoM (2.4% YoY), matching the Bloomberg consensus median. It assigns roughly 50% odds to a 0.2% MoM core print, 30% odds to 0.3%, and 20% odds to 0.1%. Core goods inflation, positive again in July, should keep contributing into August, tempered by used-auto deflation. College tuition growth should ease after boosting July's print, while airline fares inflation stays elevated on high oil prices. A 0.23% reading implies 1.7% three-month annualized core growth, below the Fed's 2% target, signaling moderate rather than hot momentum. MUFG's base case is that a 0.2% print drives a 4-6bp rates rally, since it views the pre-CPI selloff as driven mainly by non-US factors, the ECB hike and oil moves. A 0.3% print would push September hike odds toward 90% and could produce a unanimous 12-0 FOMC hike vote led by Warsh. A 0.1% print would ease hike odds to a coin flip, keep the Fed on hold with at most 2 dissents, and spark a 7-11bp rally.
